Definition: to root, i.e. strike into the soil, or (by implication) to pluck from it
BiblicalUsage: 1) to uproot, take root, deal with the roots; 1a) (Piel) to root up, root out; 1b) (Pual) to be rooted up or out (of produce); 1c) (Poel) to take root; 1d) (Poal) to take root; 1e) (Hiphil) to take root, cause to take root
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
